levels.hospitalite.intro: The door stands open to those who come back. The guardian tower welcomes them.
levels.hospitalite.subtitle: The open door
levels.hospitalite.title: Hospitality
levels.humilite.intro: The tallest tower is the one that knows how to bow.
levels.humilite.subtitle: The tower that bows

levels.parole.intro: A promise carved in stone does not fade.
levels.parole.subtitle: A promise of stone

proverbs.threshold: Stone remembers the hands that laid it.
proverbs.hospitalite: A house without a door is only one more wall.
proverbs.parole: What your mouth sets down, your hands must carry.
proverbs.anciens: The one who walked before you knows which stone slips.
proverbs.patience: The mountain does not hurry, and still it reaches the sky.
proverbs.pardon: A mended bridge carries further than one never broken.
proverbs.humilite: Bow your head at the door: low doorways guard great houses.
proverbs.epilogue: What we build for others ends up carrying us.
story.prologue.intro: Dawn finds the village empty. The tower of his fathers has split, and the valley holds its breath.
story.hospitalite.intro: A traveller waits at the edge of the void, no path before him. The guest's road is laid before your own.
story.parole.intro: A child is waiting for the bridge promised last winter. A shortcut opens; Turpal does not take it.
story.anciens.intro: The old man walks slowly among the graves. It is not for him to quicken his step.
story.patience.intro: The lake keeps the sky upside down. Some doors wait not for a hand, but for the moon.
story.pardon.intro: The tower split on the day of a quarrel no one can retell. The two halves will not meet on their own.
story.humilite.intro: Above the clouds, snow erases names. For others to climb, one must know how to step down.
story.epilogue.intro: The towers answer one another again from slope to slope. Turpal sits down, and what surrounds him is no longer silence.
